correctness.rationale: Analytic proof verifies positive real beta shapes, strict-majority normalization and both adjacent parity identities. Exact even increment integrates a sign-changing binomial polynomial and has factor \(m(\alpha-\beta)+\alpha+2m+1>0\). Symmetrized Beta density proves the limiting strict gain. Integer \((2,1)\) summation establishes first strict-even improvement at \(n=10\). Standard-library rational verification completed 444 finite checks, not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2025 social-influence theorem explicitly leaves finite-size majority improvement nonuniform; the strict-even electorate is a natural unresolved regime because ties are counted as failures. The result gives all-shape monotonicity within the even sizes, an unavoidable parity sawtooth, a finite unique benchmark crossing, and an exact minimum-free-electorate threshold for the smallest integer zealot imbalance. These describe whether adding voters can worsen and when it eventually improves collective correctness, a central voter-system design question rather than an arbitrary numeric slice.
